title: LTB-REMEDIATE-CF4: contain Flying V toolpath routes before G-code generation
intent: On base bc0ae6c8566fdc6b6f2e88513ceb217f4574e706, refuse the three unauthenticated Flying V /toolpath routes with the existing flying_v_body readiness record before generation. Do not qualify the generator, add authentication, wire the depth validator, or start the CF-2 inventory.
behavior_change: POST /api/cam/guitar/flying_v/toolpath/control_cavity, /neck_pocket, and /pickup change from HTTP 200 with a G-code program to HTTP 422 GENERATOR_READINESS_BLOCKED while flying_v_body remains REVIEW_REQUIRED. GET /spec and POST /validate are unchanged.

diff_articulation.what_changed: The three Flying V toolpath handlers call _readiness_gate("flying_v_body") as their first executable statement, before the lazy import, pickup normalization, spec load, and generator call. The readiness note records the historical 200 responses and G/M counts 394, 117, and 337, and states that the record stays REVIEW_REQUIRED. The /gcode-suffix inventory comment no longer claims to cover every guitar manufacturing route.
diff_articulation.why: Those three routes returned G-code to unauthenticated requests and were invisible to path.endswith("/gcode") discovery. They reach the same pocket_generator as the already-gated body route, so they use the existing flying_v_body key.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: POST /api/cam/guitar/flying_v/body/gcode was already gated and authenticated. The /toolpath handlers are a separate unauthenticated surface and were still emitting.
diff_articulation.what_did_not_change: No READY or QUALIFIED state. No second readiness key. No authentication change. The depth validator stays unwired. GET /spec and POST /validate are unchanged. P-1, P-2, and P-3 behavior is unchanged. CF-3 logging and the CF-2 inventory are not in this patch. No physical machine execution.
diff_articulation.why_structural_extraction: Not an extraction. The three handlers call the existing readiness gate.

proofs: Each of the three handlers has _readiness_gate("flying_v_body") as its first executable statement. A handler that normalizes pickup before the gate fails that check.

A default POST to each route returns HTTP 422 with detail.code GENERATOR_READINESS_BLOCKED, detail.route flying_v_body, and detail.generator_readiness REVIEW_REQUIRED. The three bodies are identical. No program records and no attachment.
Spies on load_flying_v_spec and the three pocket generators record zero calls. Deleting the flying_v_body record returns UNKNOWN, not a program.

The live census is exactly the three POST routes whose response model is the Flying V ToolpathResponse. A synthetic POST /toolpath/stealth with that model is discovered even though the path does not contain gcode. GET /spec and POST /validate are excluded.
flying_v_body stays REVIEW_REQUIRED. All four Flying V emission paths import app.cam.flying_v, which re-exports pocket_generator. The router does not import manufacturing-output or asset authority.
verification.hardware: No physical-machine execution. No generated program was sent to a machine.
